In summary, our research is concerned with

the characterization of the enzyme S-nitrosogluthathione reductases (GSNORs) from Brassica and Lactuca spp, which is the key enzyme involved in S-nitrosylation and S-glutathionylation of proteins in plants, as well as in the regulation of nitric oxide homeostasis.
the identification and characterization of GSNOR from important crops, and the elucidation of its function in the regulation of nitric oxide homeostasis.
the characterization of two GSNORs from two important crop species and with their role in the regulation of nitric oxide metabolism in plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both GSNORs are important enzymes for plant development, growth and response to stress.
GSNOR is an enzyme with a dual role, both in the detoxification of S-nitric oxide metabolites and in the generation of reactive oxygen species.
GSNOR is involved in the regulation of nitric oxide homeostasis and in the plant response to abiotic and/or biotic stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GSNOR enzyme is an important component of plant defense mechanisms and that its role is not limited to the regulation of GSNO levels.
GSNOR is an important player in plant growth and defense against pathogen infection.
GSNOR is involved in the regulation of GSNO levels in plant tissues and that its activity is modulated in response to developmental stages as well as biotic stresses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GSNOR enzyme has a high capacity to catalyze the reduction of S-nitrogliutathione in the intracellular compartment and its activity and gene expression are developmentally regulated.
GSNO is a key regulator in plant development and its homeostasis is controlled by GSNOR, which is a key regulator for S-nitroglutathione metabolism.
GSNOR is involved in the regulation of plant growth and development, but its role is not limited to the control of nitric oxide signaling.
